items.stem: Why do transformers add positional information to token embeddings?

options.text: Self-attention alone is order-agnostic, so position must be encoded explicitly
options.rationale: Correct: without it the model cannot tell word order.
Positional encoding does not change vocabulary.
That is unrelated to positional encoding.
It is about order, not compression.

items.explanation: Correct: without it the model cannot tell word order.

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to fine-tune a smaller model instead of prompting a large one? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Lower, more predictable inference cost at scale
options.rationale: Correct: a small fine-tuned model is cheaper to serve.

options.text: You have enough labelled data for the specific task
options.rationale: Correct: labelled data makes fine-tuning effective.

options.text: You have no task data at all
options.rationale: Without data, fine-tuning has nothing to learn from.

options.text: You need the broadest possible general knowledge with zero setup
options.rationale: That favours prompting a large general model.

items.explanation: Correct: a small fine-tuned model is cheaper to serve.

items.stem: Why can aggressive lowercasing and punctuation stripping hurt an NLP model?

options.text: It can erase meaning, such as distinguishing 'US' from 'us'

options.rationale: It does not always help and can hurt.

options.text: It is required by all tokenisers
options.rationale: Modern subword tokenisers do not require it.
